_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for United Kingdom covering Celtic Britons, Roman Britain (43-410 CE), Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy, Viking Danelaw, Norman Conquest 1066, Plantagenet dynasty, Magna Carta 1215, Hundred Years War, Wars of the Roses, Tudor dynasty (Henry VIII Reformation/Church of England, Elizabeth I Spanish Armada 1588), Stuart period (Union of Crowns 1603, English Civil War 1642-51/Cromwell, Glorious Revolution 1688), Acts of Union 1707 (Great Britain), British Empire (largest in history, 'sun never sets', 1/4 world population, decolonization), Industrial Revolution (first industrialized nation), Napoleonic Wars (Trafalgar 1805/Wellington Waterloo 1815), Victorian era (1837-1901, imperial zenith), WWI (1M dead), WWII (Battle of Britain/Blitz, Churchill), welfare state (NHS 1948), Suez Crisis 1956 (end of empire), Troubles (Northern Ireland 1968-98), Thatcher era (1979-90), devolution (Scotland/Wales/NI 1990s), Good Friday Agreement 1998, Iraq War 2003, Brexit referendum 2016 (Leave 51.9%)/exit EU Jan 31 2020, COVID, cost-of-living crisis.

religion.note: Church of England (Anglican, established church, monarch Supreme Governor, 16th century Reformation Henry VIII broke from Rome, 39 Articles, episcopal polity, Canterbury/York archbishops, ~12M members but attendance ~1M, declining); Church of Scotland (Presbyterian, established, Calvinist, John Knox); Catholic (~5M, Irish immigration, converts, recusancy history, emancipation 1829, Westminster Cathedral); rapid secularization post-WWII (especially 1960s+, 'Christian country' debate, church attendance collapsed); Commonwealth immigration brought Hinduism/Sikhism/Islam (Partition refugees 1947, Windrush 1948+, 1970s Ugandan Asians, 2000s+ Eastern Europe); Jewish community (~290k, Sephardic 17th century readmission, Ashkenazi 19th century, East End, Kindertransport, declining); 2021 census: Christianity minority for first time, No religion 37%; religious tolerance tradition but Islamophobia/antisemitism issues

ethnic_groups.name: White British
ethnic_groups.notes: English/Scottish/Welsh/Northern Irish (identity complex, England 56M/Scotland 5.4M/Wales 3.1M/NI 1.9M); 'British' identity debated (imperial legacy, devolution weakened, Brexit divided); English dominant (86% of UK); Scots (independence referendum 2014 45% Yes, SNP dominance until 2024); Welsh (language revival, Plaid Cymru); Northern Irish (Protestant/Unionist vs Catholic/Nationalist, Troubles legacy, Good Friday Agreement); class system historically rigid (aristocracy/gentry/working class, accent markers, public schools/Oxbridge, weakened but persists); Brexit (2016, 51.9% Leave, England/Wales Leave, Scotland/NI Remain, generational/educational divide)

ethnic_groups.name: Asian/Asian British
ethnic_groups.notes: Indian (~1.8M, Partition 1947+, East African expulsion 1970s Ugandan Asians, professionals/Leicester, Rishi Sunak first PM 2022-24), Pakistani (~1.2M, post-Partition, Bradford/Birmingham, working class, grooming gangs scandal Rotherham/Rochdale, Islamophobia), Bangladeshi (~450k, 1971 independence, East London/Tower Hamlets, fish-and-chips shops), Chinese (~450k, 19th century laborers, Hong Kong 1997/BNO 2020-22 ~140k, restaurants/students); model minority stereotype (except Pakistanis/Bangladeshis disadvantaged); Hindu (~1M), Sikh (~520k, Punjabi, significant political integration)

ethnic_groups.name: Black/Black British
ethnic_groups.notes: Caribbean (~600k, Windrush generation 1948-71 invited to rebuild post-war, 'No Irish No Blacks No Dogs', Notting Hill riots 1958, Brixton riots 1981, Windrush scandal 2018-present ~83 deported/died, Stephen Lawrence murder 1993/inquiry institutional racism); African (~1.5M, 1990s-2000s, Nigerian/Ghanaian/Somali/Zimbabwean, more recent, higher education); Black Lives Matter 2020 (Bristol Colston statue toppled); Metropolitan Police racism debates; disproportionate stop-and-search; music (grime, UK garage, Stormzy/Skepta); first Black British woman in Parliament 1987 (Diane Abbott)

ethnic_groups.name: Mixed/Multiple
ethnic_groups.notes: Fastest-growing category; mixed families increasingly common; identity complex

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Arab (~400k, Iraq/Yemen/Syria), Polish (~700k, post-EU 2004 accession, largest foreign-born group until Brexit), Romanian (~430k), Irish (historically millions, Great Famine 1845-52, 'No Irish' discrimination 19th century, now integrated, dual citizenship common, ~600k Irish-born); Roma/Travellers (~200k, discrimination); EU migration (2004-20, Eastern European, construction/NHS/hospitality, Brexit friction, many left); Hong Kong BNO (2020-22, ~140k fled National Security Law, largest recent immigration wave); refugees (Syrian ~20k, Afghan ~20k, Ukrainian ~200k 2022+); Channel crossings (asylum seekers, Rwanda plan controversy)

independence.from: Continuous sovereignty (Acts of Union 1707 created Kingdom of Great Britain from England+Scotland; 1801 added Ireland; 1922 Irish Free State left leaving Northern Ireland, became United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland)

country_profile.notes_unique: British Empire (largest in history, 1920s peak 35.5M km² ~24% land/412M people ~20% world pop, 'sun never sets', colonies on every continent, decolonization 1947-80s, Commonwealth 56 nations legacy, imperial nostalgia/guilt divide British identity); Industrial Revolution (birthplace, 18th-19th century, steam engine/railways/factories/coal, Manchester/Birmingham/Glasgow, 'workshop of the world', urbanization, Dickensian poverty, social reforms, trade unions); Parliamentary democracy (mother of parliaments, Westminster system, Magna Carta 1215 limited monarchy, Glorious Revolution 1688 constitutional monarchy, unwritten constitution, two-party system Conservative/Labour, House of Commons/Lords, first-past-the-post, votes for women 1918/28); WWII (Battle of Britain 1940, London Blitz, Dunkirk evacuation, Churchill 'finest hour', D-Day 1944, rationing until 1954, 'won the war lost the empire', 450k dead, national mythology); Brexit (June 23 2016 referendum 51.9% Leave, Article 50 March 2017, Theresa May/Boris Johnson negotiations, exit Jan 31 2020, transition ended Dec 31 2020, most significant constitutional change since 1973, trade deals, immigration end of free movement, 'taking back control', Northern Ireland Protocol tensions, Scotland independence debate resurgence, generational divide young=Remain, economic impacts unclear); NHS (National Health Service 1948, Attlee, Aneurin Bevan, universal healthcare 'free at point of use', beloved institution, 75th anniversary 2023, underfunding/staff shortages crises); London (global financial center, Canary Wharf/City, 9M metro, most visited European city, multicultural 37% foreign-born, center of power 1000+ years, Tower/Parliament/Buckingham Palace, Black Cab/double-decker bus/Underground); Royal Family (constitutional monarchy, King Charles III since Sept 8 2022, Elizabeth II reigned 70 years 1952-2022 longest British monarch, William Prince of Wales heir, Diana 'People's Princess' death 1997, Harry/Meghan Megxit 2020, jubilee celebrations, tourism draw £1.8B, republicanism minority); Class system (historically rigid, aristocracy/gentry/working class, accent as class marker RP/Cockney/regional, public schools Eton/Harrow/Westminster, Oxbridge dominance, social mobility debates, 'toff' stereotype, weakened post-WWII but persist); Scottish independence (SNP rise, 2014 referendum 45% Yes/55% No, Brexit reignited debate, Sturgeon/Salmond, 2024 SNP collapse after scandals, unresolved constitutional question); Northern Ireland (Troubles 1968-98, 3,500 dead, IRA/UVF, Bloody Sunday 1972, Hunger Strikes 1981 Bobby Sands, Good Friday Agreement 1998 power-sharing, peace process Nobel Prize, Brexit Protocol tensions, 2024 power-sharing restored after 2-year collapse); Shakespeare (1564-1616, greatest writer in English, 37 plays, Globe Theatre, Hamlet/Macbeth/Romeo, 'invented' 1700+ words, cultural touchstone); Beatles (1960s Liverpool, John/Paul/George/Ringo, 'British Invasion', most successful band ever, cultural revolution); Premier League (richest football league, global audience, Manchester United/Liverpool/Arsenal, 'football invented here'); BBC (public broadcaster, TV license fee, impartiality debates, Dr Who/Sherlock/Top Gear); Tea culture (afternoon tea, cuppa, 100M cups daily, British identity marker); English language (global lingua franca, colonial legacy, 1.5B speakers, soft power); Universities (Oxford 1096/Cambridge 1209, Russell Group, international students 600k+); Monarchy continuity (1000+ years, constitutional since 1688, ceremonial, State Opening Parliament, royal weddings/funerals national events); 33 UNESCO World Heritage Sites

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Keir Starmer
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Labour; landslide victory July 4, 2024 (411 seats, Conservative collapse to 121 seats worst since 1832); former Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP, CPS 2008-13); barrister/human rights lawyer; knighted; left-wing youth, now centrist 'changed Labour' (purged Corbynites); 'Mr Rules' boring persona; pro-EU but accepted Brexit; 'missions' policy (growth/NHS/crime/energy/education); early challenges: winter fuel cuts unpopular, freebies scandal, two-tier policing riots Aug 2024, business community skeptical; majority 174 but Labour vote share only 33.7% (FPTP distortion, Reform UK split right)

head_of_state.name: King Charles III
head_of_state.title: King of the United Kingdom
head_of_state.notes: Succeeded mother Elizabeth II (died Sept 8, 2022, 96 years old, 70-year reign longest British monarch); waited entire life as heir (73 years, longest); married Camilla Queen Consort (now Queen, Diana ghost); environmentalist (Prince's Trust, organic farming, architecture critic, 'meddling'); slimmed-down monarchy plan; cancer diagnosis Feb 2024 (working through treatment); William Prince of Wales heir; coronation May 2023 (scaled-down, multifaith, Commonwealth emphasis); constitutional role (sign laws, appoint PM, weekly audience)

former_leaders.name: Rishi Sunak
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; first British Asian/Hindu PM (historic); youngest PM 20th/21st century (42); ex-Chancellor; replaced Liz Truss after 49-day chaos; stabilized economy but inherited 'broken' party (5th PM in 6 years, scandals, cost-of-living crisis); lost July 2024 election catastrophically (Tory wipeout to 121 seats, worst result since 1832, 14 years in power ended, Reform UK split vote); D-Day Normandy gaffe (left early, campaign disaster); wealthy (wife Akshata Murty billionaire heiress), out-of-touch image; technocratic but politically inept

former_leaders.name: Liz Truss
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; shortest-serving PM (49 days, outlasted by lettuce, Daily Star joke); won leadership vs Sunak on right-wing tax cuts; 'mini-budget' Sept 23, 2022 (Kwasi Kwarteng Chancellor, £45B unfunded tax cuts, markets tanked, gilt yields spiked, pound crashed, mortgage crisis, U-turned, sacked Kwarteng, resigned Oct 20); Queen Elizabeth II died 2 days into premiership (Sept 8); political suicide, destroyed Tory credibility, economic chaos; book tour defending record; jokes about lettuce

former_leaders.name: Boris Johnson
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; 'Get Brexit Done' (2019 landslide 80-seat majority); COVID response (late lockdowns, 150k+ deaths, vaccine rollout success, Partygate scandal broke lockdown rules, Sue Gray report, fined by police, lied to Parliament); Dominic Cummings aide (drove to Durham lockdown, kept him, undermined credibility); 2022: cascading scandals (Chris Pincher groping, lied, ministers resigned en masse July 2022, forced out); Ukraine war (strong support Zelenskyy, supplied weapons); chaotic/populist, Eton/Oxford, classics scholar, journalist, Mayor of London 2008-16; affair/children scandals (5 wives/mistresses, unknown # children); Churchill biographer; polarizing (Remainers hated, Brexiteers loved)

former_leaders.name: Theresa May
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; succeeded Cameron post-Brexit; 'Brexit means Brexit', triggered Article 50 March 2017; 2017 election disaster (lost majority, DUP confidence-and-supply, weakened); Brexit negotiations (Chequers plan, backstop, rejected 3 times by Parliament, 'meaningful votes'), EU extended deadlines, resigned May 2019 (tears); 'strong and stable' / 'fields of wheat' memes; hostile environment immigration; first female PM since Thatcher but failed

former_leaders.name: David Cameron
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; coalition with LibDems 2010-15 (Nick Clegg Deputy PM, austerity, tuition fees betrayal); 2015 majority (unexpected, SNP surge Scotland, Ed Miliband lost); Brexit referendum June 23, 2016 (promised to appease Tory right, expected Remain to win, 51.9% Leave, Cameron resigned next day, 'greatest political blunder'); modernized Tories ('hug a hoodie', gay marriage 2013); Eton/Oxford, 'Notting Hill set', pig scandal (unauthorized biography); Libya intervention 2011; returned as Foreign Secretary 2023-24 under Sunak (made Lord)

former_leaders.name: Gordon Brown
former_leaders.notes: Labour; Chancellor 1997-2007 (10 years, boom years, 'ended boom and bust' [didn't], sold gold at bottom); succeeded Blair (no election, 'bottled' 2007 election); Financial Crisis 2008 (Northern Rock, bank bailouts, recession, 'saved the world' gaffe); lost 2010 (bigoted woman incident hurt); 'Stalinist', 'psychologically flawed' (Blair); Scottish, serious, unlucky timing

former_leaders.name: Tony Blair
former_leaders.notes: Labour; landslide 1997 (179-seat majority, 'Things Can Only Get Better', ended 18 years Tory rule, New Labour 'Third Way', modernized party); 3 election wins (1997/2001/2005); Iraq War 2003 (Bush ally, WMD false claim, Chilcot Inquiry 2016 'not last resort', 179 UK dead, destroyed legacy, anti-war protests largest in UK history 1M+); Good Friday Agreement 1998 (Northern Ireland peace, Nobel Prize Mo Mowlam); devolution (Scotland/Wales 1999, mayors); minimum wage; NHS investment; Kosovo 1999 (humanitarian intervention); Afghanistan 2001; 'Cool Britannia'; Cherie lawyer; resigned 2007 (Gordon Brown succession), Middle East envoy, hugely wealthy (speeches/consulting, £80M), polarizing (war criminal vs greatest PM), knighted 2022 (petition against), Labour centrists vs Corbynites civil war; charismatic, presentational politics

former_leaders.name: Margaret Thatcher
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; first female PM (11 years, longest 20th century); 'Iron Lady'; neoliberalism (privatization, deregulation, anti-union, Thatcherism); Miners' Strike 1984-85 (crushed NUM, closed pits, devastated communities, Orgreave); Falklands War 1982 (Argentina invaded, UK won, jingoism, saved career); Poll Tax 1990 (riots, resignation trigger); IRA Brighton bombing 1984 (survived, 5 killed); right-to-buy council houses (created property-owning democracy, housing crisis legacy); Section 28 (banned 'promoting homosexuality', homophobic); special relationship Reagan/Bush; Brussels speech 1988 (Eurosceptic); ousted by own party Nov 1990 (Michael Heseltine challenge, Geoffrey Howe resignation speech, tearful exit); died 2013; most polarizing PM (worshipped by right, despised by left, 'Ding Dong the Witch is Dead' charted, regions never recovered); defined an era

former_leaders.name: Winston Churchill
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; WWII leader (1940-45, 'We shall fight on the beaches', 'finest hour', rallied nation, Blitz/Battle of Britain, D-Day, defeat of Nazis, national hero, Nobel Literature 1953); voted out 1945 (Attlee landslide, wanted welfare state); return 1951-55 (peacetime less successful, stoke, aging); imperialism (India independence opposed, Gallipoli WWI disaster 1915, Bengal Famine 1943 culpability debated); Britain's greatest figure (2002 BBC poll), statues, £5 note; cigars/V-sign/hats; died 1965 (state funeral)
